source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul pentru 7 noiembrie — «Sfântul Cuvios Lazăr din Muntele Galision»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Νοεμβρίου — «Όσιος Λάζαρος ο Θαυματουργός, ο Γαλλησιώτης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same man: the son of Nicetas and Irene from a village near Magnesia, who kept a pillar on Mount Galesion by Ephesus. It prints a proper apolytikion that names him and a kontakion that addresses him as our father and shepherd, both taken here; the Οἶκος on the same page is not a kind the schema holds and is not drafted. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (25 September 2026).

hymns.text: Cu rugăciunile cele cu priveghere, întru curgerile lacrimilor stâlpul ţi-ai udat şi cu suspinurile cele din adâncuri, spre însutite osteneli, l-ai făcut roditor. Şi ai fost păstor, tuturor dând iertare, Cuvioase Lazăr, părintele nostru, roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Lazăr din Muntele Galision

english.text: With vigilant prayers thou didst water thy pillar with the streams of thy tears, and with sighs from the depths thou didst make it fruitful unto labours a hundredfold. And thou wast a shepherd, granting pardon to all; venerable Lazarus our father, pray to Christ God that our souls be saved.

hymns.text: Ταῖς ἐπαγρύπνοις προσευχαῖς, ἐν ὀχετοῖς δακρύων τὸν στῦλον κατέβρεχες· καὶ τοῖς ἐκ βάθων στεναγμοῖς, εἰς ἑκατὸν τοὺς πόνους ἐκαρποφόρησας· καὶ γέγονας ποιμήν, τοῖς προσιοῦσι νέμων συγχώρησιν, Ὅσιε Πατὴρ ἡμῶν Λάζαρε· πρέσβευε Χριστῷ τῷ Θεῷ σωθῆναι τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’ — the first hymn on the page of «Όσιος Λάζαρος ο Θαυματουργός, ο Γαλλησιώτης», and it names him and his pillar.

english.text: With sleepless prayers you drenched your pillar in streams of tears; and with groanings from the depths you made your labours bear fruit a hundredfold; and you became a shepherd, dealing out forgiveness to those who came to you, our venerable father Lazarus. Intercede with Christ our God that our souls be saved.

hymns.text: Τοὺς ὑπὲρ φύσιν σου Σοφὲ πόνους καὶ σκάμματα, αὐτοὶ οἱ Ἄγγελοι ἰδόντες κατεπλάγησαν, δι᾽ ὧν εἴληφας θεόθεν καὶ τοὺς στεφάνους, Ἀλλ᾽ ὣς ἔχων παῤῥησίαν πρὸς τὸν Κύριον, ἐκ παντοίων ἡμᾶς σῷζε περιστάσεων, ἵνα κράζωμεν, Χαίροις Πάτερ Ποιμὴν ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ — on the page of «Όσιος Λάζαρος ο Θαυματουργός, ο Γαλλησιώτης». It addresses him as wise one and as our father and shepherd and names no other saint.

english.text: Seeing your labours and your contests, which were beyond nature, O wise one, the very angels were amazed; and through them you received your crowns from God. Having then boldness before the Lord, save us from every kind of trouble, that we may cry: Rejoice, our father and shepherd.

death.note: saint.gr's head line for him, «Οσιος Λαζαρος ο Θαυματουργος, ο Γαλλησιωτης (; - 1054)», and its text: «πέθανε με αγιότητα σε βαθιά γεράματα το 1054 μ.Χ.»; the same page puts his birth in the eleventh century.
